naia.types: Naia comes in three main forms. Naia filament yarn, the original 2017 product, is continuous cellulose acetate for wovens and knits with a silk-like luster. Naia staple fiber, which Eastman showed at Premiere Vision in 2020, is cut fiber for blending with other fibers in spun yarns, mainly for knitwear. Naia Renew, available as filament and staple, is described by Eastman as 60% wood pulp and 40% certified recycled waste plastics, with the recycled content allocated by an ISCC-certified mass balance method; Naia Renew ES is a version Eastman says carries increased recycled content. Within each form, deniers, filament counts and luster levels distinguish specific yarns.
naia.fabrics: Naia filament is used in satins, crepes, charmeuse-like wovens, jacquards and linings, in blouses, dresses and eveningwear, and in fluid knits. Staple Naia blends appear in sweaters, cardigans and T-shirt knits, where Eastman highlights softness and reduced pilling. Acetate's classic role as a lining persists alongside cupro and viscose. Eastman announced H&M as the first brand to adopt Naia Renew, in a Conscious Exclusive collection. Because acetate is thermoplastic, it is also used where heat-set pleats or moire effects are wanted.
naia.quality: The label must say acetate, not Naia alone and not 'silk'. For filament wovens, look for a dense, smooth weave with no seam slippage and even luster; acetate satins with loose weaves slip at seams under stress. Test a hidden spot before using nail polish remover or perfume nearby: acetone dissolves acetate, and a genuine acetate fabric is marked by it. For Naia Renew, ask how the 40% recycled content is allocated: under mass balance, the recycled molecules are credited on paper across production, not physically traceable in each fiber. Eastman lists ISCC and GRS-related certifications; confirm the certificate covers the product.
pros: Acetate filament gives a silk-like luster and drape at a lower price than silk.
It dries faster and wrinkles less than viscose because acetylation reduces water uptake.
Eastman reports TUV AUSTRIA 'OK biodegradable' marks for soil and freshwater and 'OK compost' for industrial composting.
Naia Renew uses recycled waste plastics as a feedstock for acetyl chemicals, according to Eastman.
cons: Acetone, some nail polish removers and some solvents dissolve or mark acetate.
It is weaker than viscose or polyester and loses strength when wet, so it abrades and tears more easily.
Heat can glaze or melt it, making ironing risky.
Mass balance allocation means recycled content in Naia Renew is an accounting credit rather than a measurable share of each fiber.
naia.impact: Eastman's claims are that Naia production recovers its solvents in a closed loop, and that Naia Renew has a lower carbon footprint than standard Naia; it also cites a study with the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution showing Naia disintegrating and biodegrading in the ocean within months. Independent evidence adds context. In a 2019 washing study (Yang and colleagues, Environmental Pollution), acetate fabric released the most microfibers of the three fabrics tested, up to about 74,800 per square meter per wash. A 2023 study (Tan and colleagues) found cellulose acetate tow and film lost under 3% of weight after 16 weeks in river water or seawater, showing that degradation depends strongly on degree of substitution, form and microbial conditions. Biodegradability claims should therefore be read against their stated test conditions.
naia.care: Hand wash in cool water or use a delicate cycle at 30 C in a mesh bag, with mild detergent; many acetate garments are labeled dry clean only, and linings in tailored garments should be dry cleaned with the outer fabric. Never wring or twist. Roll in a towel and hang or dry flat, away from heat; do not tumble dry. Iron at the lowest setting (the one-dot range, about 110 C) on the reverse with a press cloth, because acetate glazes and can melt. Keep acetone, nail polish remover and some perfumes and alcohol-based sprays away. Store on padded hangers to avoid shoulder marks.
faq: Neither exactly. It is made from wood pulp cellulose that is chemically modified with acetyl groups, so it is a manufactured cellulose ester. Labels call it acetate. It behaves partly like a cellulose and partly like a thermoplastic.
Is Naia the same as silk?

No. Acetate imitates silk's luster and drape, but it is a wood-derived manufactured fiber. It is weaker than silk, especially when wet, and is damaged by acetone and high heat. Content labels must say acetate.

Eastman reports certifications for biodegradation in soil and freshwater and composting in industrial facilities, plus a marine study. Independent research shows acetate degradation varies strongly with conditions, and garments with dyes, blends or threads may behave differently, so check the stated test conditions.
What does 'mass balance' mean for Naia Renew?

Eastman feeds recycled plastic into its chemical production and allocates the recycled share to certain products through ISCC-certified bookkeeping. The recycled content is real at site level but cannot be measured in any individual fiber.
notable: A drop of acetone on a hidden seam allowance is a classic home test: acetate softens or dissolves while viscose, cotton and silk do not.
Eastman cites a Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution study in which Naia disintegrated and biodegraded in seawater within months.
